accepted_static_properties: SIGTERM/SIGINT share a flag-only handler, avoiding exceptions between Popen and ownership bookkeeping. Active-child monitor observes the flag and takes the failed cleanup path.

Child starts a separate session; pending/spawning metadata precedes Popen; pid/pgid/sid/start_ticks are saved before monitoring. Cleanup checks the live leader identity before group signals. WNOWAIT retains leader identity until owned group empties, then reaps. Unconfirmed cleanup remains a failure.

Cleanup targets only the proven owned process group with SIGTERM then bounded SIGKILL escalation. SIGKILL/host loss/uninterruptible waits/unavailable storage are explicitly outside safety guarantees; pending state refuses automatic continuation.

Nonblocking flock serializes invocations. Index0 refuses an existing state/result, initialization is exclusive, failed/pending/completed states cannot resume, and exact prior receipt hashes/command/index/status plus baseline/deadline/start are checked before continuing.

Original disk baseline/deadline/start are retained across successful-prefix invocations. Fixed limit values require2GiB sampled groupRSS,1GiB increment,17GiB initial disk and16GiB remaining disk/memory,Go2 threads/jobs,180second reserve and195second prelaunch cutoff. Manifest duration is at most1200seconds.

Measurement includes wholeR and own probe/cache/tmp/gopath plus own-S extras; overlap refuses and docs are counted once. Fixed Go environment override conflicts refuse. Pre/post input hashes remain checked even on command failure.

Atomic metadata writes fsync temporary file and containing directory; per-step receipts are no-clobber. Closed stdout OSError is caught, so the intended active-signal path does not depend on a reader.

The prepared fixture is Python-only, uses a fresh own-probe directory, successful prefix then one child/grandchild group, closes stdout and signals only the guard, checks durable failed state/cleanup/readsets, then tests failed resume and index0 reset refusal. It does not constitute executed evidence.
